# OpenAPI 3.x and Swagger 2.0 counters, YAML or JSON, for a rule with the prompt file-body-contract:
# one per line, label TAB pattern (Java regex). The [ignore] line blanks YAML comments (a whole line,
# or from a # after a blank) and the body of a block scalar (the lines below a | or > that are deeper
# than its key, past a list item's dash, as deep as the first of them; the key stays, an empty scalar
# blanks no sibling key), so a description that quotes a path or a "type: object" does not count. A
# double-quoted string that holds a # is blanked whole, so its # opens no comment: "Fixes #12" in a
# one-line JSON spec blanks nothing after it (a string not closed on its line ends there). A key
# that is quoted and holds a : opens no block scalar. A key counts with or
# without JSON quotes, so a minified JSON spec counts too. "operations" counts a get, put, post,
# delete, options, head, patch or trace key one level below a path key (/orders:) in YAML, read by
# its indentation: the path item's summary, description, servers, parameters, $ref and x- keys and
# their bodies may stand before and between the operations, so a schema property named options or
# head does not count, nor a webhook's or a callback's operation. In a JSON spec on one line it
# counts an operation whose first key is tags, summary, operationId, parameters, requestBody,
# responses, security, servers or callbacks (one that starts with its description is not seen).
# "parameters (approx)" an in: of one of the six locations, which an apiKey security scheme's in:
# (header, query or cookie) is too.
# OpsFactPatternsTest pins every case; ProfileFactPatternsLinearityTest measures that every pattern
# reads linearly.
[ignore] comments and block scalars
paths
operations (approx)
operationIds
parameters (approx)
$ref references
object schemas
security schemes
deprecated operations and fields
